programme: TFEB and ATF6 are the two arms of the organelle-stress/proteostasis response: ATF6 is the ER-stress sensor of the unfolded-protein response, and TFEB is the master transcriptional driver of lysosome biogenesis and autophagy that clears what the UPR cannot fold. The two are known to cooperate — ATF6-branch ER stress feeds into TFEB-dependent autophagic clearance of the resulting misfolded-protein/organelle burden — so together they describe a single stress-clearance module rather than two unrelated factors.
role_in_a: In COVID-19, SARS-CoV-2 replication overloads the ER with viral glycoprotein synthesis and manipulates host membrane trafficking (M protein disperses the trans-Golgi network, PMID 42085452), engaging the UPR (PMID 41798766, PMID 38785529) with ATF6 among the branches implicated. The virus also actively degrades TFEB to blunt autophagic clearance and lysosomal defense, and reversing that degradation is proposed as a host-directed therapy (PMID 40465712); dysregulated TFEB-autophagy-lysosome signaling has separately been tied to acute immunopathology and Long COVID (PMID 41394849).
role_in_b: In ischemic stroke, oxygen-glucose deprivation produces the same two stresses in neurons and glia: misfolded-protein ER stress, where ATF6 activation is neuroprotective and confers long-term benefit after permanent ischemia (PMID 40259100) and features in proteostasis dynamics in neuron/glia co-culture models (PMID 42372148); and lysosomal/autophagic stress, where TFEB-dependent autophagy limits neuronal damage (PMID 41876744) and ferroptosis (PMID 41272418), and its disruption in newly formed oligodendrocytes drives aberrant repair (PMID 42268879).
shared_axis: Two mechanistically unrelated insults — viral protein overproduction in COVID-19 and ischemic energy failure in stroke — both overwhelm the ER's folding capacity and the cell's clearance machinery, so both diseases independently converge on activating the same ATF6-UPR/TFEB-autophagy checkpoint as a survival response, which is what a blood-derived regulatory signature would pick up in each condition separately.
reasoning: Both factors are consistently concordant (8/12 groups, not single-view), have real Open Targets association in at least one disease each (TFEB in both), and each is independently backed by multiple disease-specific, non-review papers in COVID-19 and in stroke — that is direct retrieved placement, satisfying the bar for strong. But nothing retrieved connects COVID-19 and stroke to each other through this axis (the one joint TFEB hit is about ALS/FTD, the joint ATF6-adjacent hit about sepsis/ARDS), so the shared axis is inferred from parallel disease biology rather than a stated fact, which caps the verdict at supported rather than established.
support: 41394849 (TFEB-autophagy-lysosome dysregulation in acute COVID-19 and Long COVID); 40465712 (viral degradation of TFEB and its reversal as host-directed COVID therapy); 41876744 (TFEB-dependent autophagy limits neuronal damage, ischemia-relevant model); 42268879 (TFEB/autophagy disruption in oligodendrocyte formation after injury); 41272418 (TFEB-lysosomal pathway regulates neuronal ferroptosis in a stroke model); 42085452 (coronavirus M protein disrupts ER/Golgi trafficking, upstream of ATF6 activation); 41798766 (UPR modulation has antiviral effects in coronavirus infection); 38785529 (UPR activation mechanism during coronavirus infection); 40259100 (ATF6 activation is neuroprotective after permanent cerebral ischemia); 42372148 (UPR/proteostasis dynamics in neuron-glia co-culture, neurodegeneration-relevant).
how_to_falsify: In PBMCs or monocytes drawn from COVID-19 and ischemic-stroke cohorts, pharmacologically block ATF6 (e.g., Ceapin-A7) and TFEB nuclear translocation (e.g., via mTORC1 reactivation) and ask whether the two diseases' concordant target genes (HSPA5/BiP, DNAJB9, CDKN2A for ATF6; SERPINE1, CD40LG for TFEB) lose their correlated induction pattern; if blocking these two factors does not collapse the shared target signature, or if the same target concordance persists in a disease pair with no documented UPR/autophagy involvement, the proposed module is not what is carrying the concordance.
caveats: Both tissues sampled are blood, and the comparison rests on only 12 patient-group comparisons from 4 independent cohort pairs, a modest base; TFEB and ATF6 are each supported in 8 of 12, well above the single-view exclusions but not near-universal. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed the classic immune transcription factors of blood (STAT1/3/5A, CIITA, JUNB, SMAD3, LEF1, E2F1, EPAS1) — meaning the obvious inflammatory story was already stripped out before this signature emerged, which is consistent with a non-immune, stress-proteostasis explanation but also means this account cannot invoke those factors even where they would seem natural. Several other concordant factors (NFIL3, TCF7, ARID5A) have their own disease-specific literature but sit on distinct axes (thromboinflammation, T-cell/Wnt signaling, ischemic preconditioning) and were left out to avoid forcing a single narrative over all twelve; roughly a third of the factors (ZBTB10, NFE2L3, TLX1, KCNIP3, CEBPE, KAT8) have no usable literature and should not be treated as evidence either way.
